name: Drazil Likes Heap
description: Drazil likes heap very much. So he created a problem with heap: There is a max heap with a height $$$h$$$ implemented on the array. The details of this heap are the following: This heap contains exactly $$$2^h - 1$$$ distinct positive non-zero integers. All integers are distinct. These numbers are stored in the array $$$a$$$ indexed from $$$1$$$ to $$$2^h-1$$$. For any $$$1 \lt i \lt 2^h$$$, $$$a[i] \lt a[\left \lfloor{\frac{i}{2}}\right \rfloor]$$$. Now we want to reduce the height of this heap such that the height becomes $$$g$$$ with exactly $$$2^g-1$$$ numbers in heap. To reduce the height, we should perform the following action $$$2^h-2^g$$$ times: Choose an index $$$i$$$, which contains an element and call the following function $$$f$$$ in index $$$i$$$: Note that we suppose that if $$$a[i]=0$$$, then index $$$i$$$ don't contain an element. After all operations, the remaining $$$2^g-1$$$ element must be located in indices from $$$1$$$ to $$$2^g-1$$$. Now Drazil wonders what's the minimum possible sum of the remaining $$$2^g-1$$$ elements. Please find this sum and find a sequence of the function calls to achieve this value.
input_specification: The first line of the input contains an integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \leq t \leq 70\,000$$$): the number of test cases. Each test case contain two lines. The first line contains two integers $$$h$$$ and $$$g$$$ ($$$1 \leq g \lt h \leq 20$$$). The second line contains $$$n = 2^h-1$$$ distinct positive integers $$$a[1], a[2], \ldots, a[n]$$$ ($$$1 \leq a[i] \lt 2^{20}$$$). For all $$$i$$$ from $$$2$$$ to $$$2^h - 1$$$, $$$a[i] \lt a[\left \lfloor{\frac{i}{2}}\right \rfloor]$$$. The total sum of $$$n$$$ is less than $$$2^{20}$$$.
output_specification: For each test case, print two lines. The first line should contain one integer denoting the minimum sum after reducing the height of heap to $$$g$$$. The second line should contain $$$2^h - 2^g$$$ integers $$$v_1, v_2, \ldots, v_{2^h-2^g}$$$. In $$$i$$$-th operation $$$f(v_i)$$$ should be called.
approach_summary: Build a Segment Tree over the array. Implement point update and associative range query operations in O(log N) time per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1329C — Drazil Likes Heap [57. Segment Tree (Point Update Range Query)]
topic_editorial.summary: Range queries and updates via Segment Tree.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The query operation is associative (e.g., sum, min, max, gcd). Any contiguous range $[L, R]$ can be decomposed into at most $O(\log N)$ canonical dyadic intervals represented by nodes in a binary tree.
topic_editorial.solution_walkthrough:
### Step 1: Tree Construction
We build a binary segment tree over array $A[1..N]$.
Each node covers a segment $[L, R]$. If $L = R$, the node stores $A[L]$. Otherwise:
$$\text{node.val} = \text{combine}(\text{left\_child.val}, \text{right\_child.val})$$

### Step 2: Point / Range Updates
To update position $pos$ with value $val$:
- Traverse down to the leaf node $[pos, pos]$.
- Update leaf value.
- Recompute ancestor values on the way back up in $O(\log N)$ time.

### Step 3: Range Query Processing
To query the associative aggregate on range $[qL, qR]$:
- If current segment $[L, R]$ is completely within $[qL, qR]$, return node value.
- If disjoint, return identity element.
- Otherwise, split and return $\text{combine}(\text{query}(left), \text{query}(right))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}((N + Q) \log N)$
  Building the segment tree takes $\mathcal{O}(N)$. Each point/range query and update traverses at most $4 \log N$ tree nodes, requiring $\mathcal{O}(\log N)$ time per query.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  A standard binary segment tree requires at most $4N$ nodes to represent elements up to index $N$.
